newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen flat-off $0.50-trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen flat-off $0.50-trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen mostly steady, instances $0.50 per cwt lower, depending on how many hogs were marketed in specific areas, according to livestock dealers.

Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices at the plant were seen steady with Tuesday's, ranging from $58.00 to $58.50. Illinois dealers said top prices could be steady to $0.50 lower, with top plant prices at $57.50 to $58.00.
Indiana hog prices were seen steady, with a top of $58.00 for hogs delivered to the plant. Ohio hogs also were seen steady, with a plant top of $55.00.
Cash hog prices could be pressured by lighter packer demand as pork prices start to slide. Pork prices were being pressured by large production.
Midday carlot pork prices were weaker, led by declines in bellies, hams and lean trimmings, according to USDA.
USDA estimated Tuesday's hog slaughter at 360,000 head, which brought the week to date estimate to 726,000 head, up 1.3 percent from a week ago and 4.6 percent above a year ago.
Also, retailers likely have already booked what they need for the first half of this month's expected pork promotions for National Pork Month, market sources said.
